(Remote, US East Coast or the same time zone. Series B. DevTools SaaS. Synthetic monitoring. 40h/week)
The best developers don’t wait for a customer to tell them something’s broken.
They catch it first, in the pull request, in staging, or in the checkout flow at 3am, before a single user notices. That instinct is Checkly’s whole reason to exist. Now that agents write and ship more and more code, they can carry that instinct too. Agents write, run, and maintain the monitoring setup that guards production, while developers stay in control. Everything is defined as code, powered by OpenTelemetry and Playwright, and versioned and reviewed like everything else that ships. From pull request to post-mortem, in one place.
AI agents are shipping more code than any team can review, and reliability is lagging behind. Checkly closes this gap. As a Support Engineer, you’ll support our most valuable customers, from modern AI companies like Mistral and resolve.ai to large engineering orgs like LinkedIn, Citi, and 1Password on that journey.
In 2024 we raised $20M in Series B funding from Balderton, CRV and Accel. We’re a remote-first startup that is low on meetings, high on productivity, and always shipping. If you love actually listening to and working with customers, working async, and keeping it lean, you’ll fit right in!
We care about building a team where people of all backgrounds are encouraged to do their best work. To achieve this we built a flexible and async-first startup environment with inclusive benefits and full transparency about how we pay.
## What you’ll do
Support has always been about solving real problems for real people. What’s changing at Checkly is how we do it: AI lets us automate routine work and assist us with troubleshooting, so we can go deeper on hard cases and bring what customers tell us straight back to the product. Here’s where you come in:
• Resolve customer issues. Debug Playwright tests (flaky selectors, timeouts, auth flows). Dig into API check failures with packet captures (PCAPs), traceroutes and timing breakdowns. Set up single sign-on (SSO) and SAML. When it’s a bug, bring engineering a clean reproduction, or open the pull request (PR) yourself.
• Build an outstanding AI support process. Our internal and external support agents already resolve 80% of tickets. You’ll help lift the bar: what the agent answers, when it hands off to a human, and how good those answers are.
• Turn tickets into product. Spot patterns across customers and bring product and engineering a reproduction. Your work becomes bug fixes and features.
• Own the docs. If you’ve answered something twice, it belongs in the docs and in the agent, so customers and AI get the same right answer.
• Work with modern tooling. We are continuously updating our workbench, and you’ll have modern tools like Plain, Linear, and Mintlify.
## This won't be the right role if you...
• Want a clear process for every situation before you act.
• Would rather code all day than talk to customers.
• See AI tools as something you’ll get around to eventually.
• Want the structure and pace of a large company.
## What you should have
You will often speak with developers who need assistance understanding if their applications work well and if not, what caused the issue. This requires a solid technical background and a genuine motivation to help and learn.
• Empathy: You love working with customers and solving their problems. Checkly is critical to them, and we genuinely want to unblock them.
• Some experience in a technical role, for example, as a developer or in technical support.
• You can read and debug JavaScript, TypeScript and Node.js code.
• You’re comfortable with HTTP, REST APIs, browser dev tools, git and CI/CD practices.
• AI is already how you work. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or similar are part of your day. You’ve built your own workflows.
• You write and speak clear, friendly English.
• You can run your own day remotely and still enjoy working with your team.
• You're based on the US East Coast or the same time zone.
## Why us?
• Transparent salary because your salary shouldn't be dictated by how good a negotiator you are. (more info below)
• Async-first (low meeting, high productivity) and transparent culture
• Stock options
• Flexible paid vacation
• Paid sick leave & up to 14 weeks of paid parental leave
• US: Medical, Dental, Vision, FSA, long- and short-term disability, life insurance, 401(k) and more
• Annual company off-site
Find out more here .
## What we pay
Fair, competitive, and transparent pay is very important for us. Therefore we work with a standardized salary calculator that includes several factors such as seniority level as well as location.
For this role, the range is
• $57,500 - $70,000 for someone in the US
• $71,910 - $87,000 for someone in US Tier 1 locations like NYC, Boston
• $43,000 - $52,000 for someone in e.g. South America

If this sounds interesting, please apply! Studies by several different sources have shown that on average men will apply for a job if they meet 60% of the application requirements. Women, non-binary people and POC will seek to match a much higher percentage of requirements before applying. If you're not sure you're the right fit, apply anyway and let us know what you bring to the table. We'd love to hear from you!

Success looks like teams that ship reliably and independently because the tools and workflows you've built make the right approach the straightforward one.
You'll work hands-on as an engineer — composing testing solutions from in-house and third-party frameworks, hardening CI/CD quality gates, writing production-quality code, and documenting the patterns and playbooks others rely on — while partnering with our Quality Engineering Lead to execute and evolve our automated testing strategy. • You have 5+ years in software engineering, with significant time as a Software Engineer in Test or Quality Engineer building systems that improve product quality.
• You have strong software engineering fundamentals and write production-quality code in at least one of Python, TypeScript, or Elixir.
• You've designed and implemented automated testing across unit, integration, API, and end-to-end layers, composing solutions from both in-house and third-party frameworks.

• You use AI and agentic coding tools as part of your day-to-day engineering.

• You approach quality through a developer-experience lens and have the judgment to know where automation pays off and where it doesn't.
• You understand quality as an engineering discipline and prefer enabling teams to own it over centralizing testing.
• You operate well with autonomy in an early-stage startup environment.
• You have an interest in AI governance and responsible AI.
## Expectations
• Partner with the Quality Engineering Lead to execute and evolve Credo AI's automated testing and quality engineering strategy.
• Compose, build, and maintain the testing frameworks, tooling, libraries, and supporting documentation that make high-quality software the default.
• Use AI and agentic coding tools to extend our testing framework, debug tests, and build AI-enabled workflows for test authoring.
• Advance automated testing maturity across our Elixir, TypeScript, and Python codebases, keeping our practices current with industry standards.
• Strengthen CI/CD pipelines and quality gates so engineering teams get fast, actionable feedback.
• Improve the developer experience around testing so that quality is easier to build in than to skip.
• Influence and coach engineers on testing strategy and effective use of frameworks and tooling, building shared ownership of quality.
• Participate in engineering reviews focused on testability, reliability, observability, and maintainability.
• Define and track quality metrics — automation coverage, test reliability, release confidence, and defect escape rates — and use them to prioritize the highest-impact work.
## Compensation
The expected base salary range for this position is $140,000-$160,000. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. The range displayed on each job posting reflects the minimum and maximum target for new hire salaries for the position in the specified location. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

Tonic.ai has been de-identifying sensitive data since 2018, and hundreds of enterprises use our products, among them eBay, American Express, UnitedHealth Group, Volvo, Qualcomm, and Commonwealth Bank. Most of them came to us with the same problem: their engineers need realistic data to build and test software, and they can’t use production data to do it.
We’re looking for someone who loves to solve complex customer problems and then immediately turns around and builds a system so that this problem solves itself next time. Moreover, this person gets to the root of why and how each customer is using Tonic so that they can maximize the value every customer is getting out of our product. The ideal Solutions Architect will be proactive, coming up with creative solutions if customers aren't getting what they need, and pressing customers when they're not doing what they need to succeed.
## Why This Role, Why Now
AI has made writing code nearly free. Knowing whether that code, and the agents built on top of it, will behave in production hasn’t gotten any easier. Agents especially need realistic, messy, data to be tested against, and basic solutions / AI slop won’t surface the failures that matter. Teams are shipping faster than their test data can keep up, and that gap is our business.
The platform is robust and scalable. What makes it valuable is someone who can walk into a customer’s environment, work out where Tonic fits in their stack and their release process, prove it in a pilot, and make it stick after the deal closes. That’s this job. You’ll work alongside our AEs before the sale and with customers’ engineering teams after it, with a direct line back to our product and engineering teams.
## What You’ll Do
• Run technical discovery with prospects’ engineering, DevOps and QA teams. Map their data sources, environments and release process, and find where Tonic fits.
• Design and demo the solution, and handle the hard technical questions: security review, deployment model, performance at scale, and how Tonic fits their CI/CD.
• Scope pilots with clear, written success criteria, then run them to a decision.
• Own onboarding after the deal closes. Deploy Tonic, connect data sources, configure de-identification and subsetting, and get the customer generating usable test data within our time-to-generation targets.
• Design test-data pipelines for agent and software testing, combining de-identified production data and synthetic data to fit each customer’s environment.
• Diagnose problems as they appear: broken foreign keys, schema drift, sensitive columns missed, jobs that won’t finish. Fix them where you can. Where you can’t, understand the issue well enough to explain it clearly to the engineer who can.
• Train customer teams so they can run Tonic without you.
• Bring field insight back to product and engineering: which features matter, which bugs are blocking deals and where the product should go next.
• Support existing customers on high-complexity issues, and work with account teams to spot expansion early.
• Turn every one-off fix into something reusable: scripts, documentation, runbooks and product improvements, so each SA can support more customers than the last.
## What We’re Looking For
• A bachelor’s degree in a technical field (computer science, engineering, information systems, math or similar), or equivalent experience.
• 3+ years in a technical customer-facing role: Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Technical Customer Success or Forward Deployed Engineer.
• Hands-on experience with relational databases and data warehouses, and with cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure or GCP). You can read a schema and tell quickly where the trouble will be.
• Working knowledge of how modern software gets built and tested: CI/CD, Docker and Kubernetes, test environments and testing frameworks.
• Comfort scripting and automating in Python and SQL. You’d rather build the fix than repeat the workaround.
• AI-native workflow. AI tools and agents are central to how you work. You know where they’re reliable and where they need your oversight.
• Ownership. You’ll often be the technical lead on an account, making sound calls without waiting to be told.
• Range. You can go deep with a DBA on one call and make the business case to a VP of Engineering on the next.
• Willingness to travel up to 25%, domestic and international.
## Nice to Haves
• Experience with agent evaluation and testing.
• Experience with test data management, data masking, or synthetic data tooling.
• Experience supporting security and compliance reviews in regulated industries like healthcare and financial services.
• Experience at an early-stage company or on a new product line.
## What Success Looks Like
In your first month, you’ll learn the platform and the delivery process and run pre- and post-sale engagements alongside your peers. By the end of your first quarter, you’ll run engagements on your own, and the scripts and runbooks you’ve written will have made your third onboarding faster than your first. After that, it’s about execution: converting pilots into customers and getting them live on time. You’ll also help shape how the SA function scales as we grow.
## Why Join
• You’ll be early in agent testing, a market that’s taking shape right now, working with some of the largest companies in the world.
• You’ll see an unusually wide range of technical environments, from startups to the Fortune 500 and from cloud-native stacks to mainframes.
• You’ll have a direct line from what you see in the field to what gets built.
• You’ll help define how the next generation of software and agents gets tested.
• Competitive compensation and equity.

Medley is an instructional support tool for multilingual learners that helps students access grade-level content. Our browser extension layers individualized reading and writing scaffolds directly onto the digital materials schools already use, including curriculum platforms, Google Docs, websites, and PDFs. Supports are tailored to a student's English proficiency level and home language, so students get the help they need in real time while staying engaged with the same rigorous content as their peers. Medley is grounded in research-backed practices and is already being used by over 50 districts across the US.
## The Opportunity
We're hiring a Technical Product Manager, Pedagogy & AI Quality to ensure that Medley’s AI-powered instructional scaffolds continue to meet our high bar for quality and user experience. You'll tighten our rubrics for what high-quality scaffolds look like for reading and writing support in the areas of both multilingual learning and special education, and across various subjects. You’ll expand upon our metrics, build upon our robust evals systems, and review processes that hold our AI to that bar.
This is a hybrid role at the intersection of pedagogy and AI product work. You'll write and test prompts, label and analyze model outputs, dig through traces and error reports, and partner closely with engineering to ship quality improvements. You will also learn and leverage the research around scaffolding high-quality instructional materials for multilingual learners at different proficiency levels, as well as accommodations and supports for students with receptive and expressive language disabilities and neurodivergent students.
You'll work closely with our head of product and engineers to ensure that Medley consistently serves teachers and students in our partner districts with scaffolds that meet the highest levels of quality. Over time, you’ll own the quality and usability of our scaffolds suite as it continues to grow to support more students with diverse needs, prioritizing product improvements and new features to better support teachers and drive student outcomes.
## What You'll Do
• Define what "excellent" looks like. Translate research-based practice in literacy, special education, and multilingual learner instruction into clear, usable quality standards for Medley scaffolds, and set targets for AI output quality.
• Track and monitor quality with a robust evals system. Build and maintain datasets, rubrics, and eval suites and conduct regular error analysis and trace review, combining human labeling, LLM-as-judge and rule-based evals.
• Refine prompts and models as needed. Write, test, and refine prompts; run model comparisons and regression tests, making changes as needed to ensure outputs are consistently meeting target metrics and passing quality thresholds.
• Stay close to our users and represent their voice in product decisions. Regularly review signals from educators, data from support tickets, product analytics, and conduct user research with students and teachers to inform product decisions.
• Prioritize and ship AI quality and scaffold-related product improvements. Maintain a prioritized backlog of AI quality and scaffold UX issues; write clear specs, and work with engineering to scope, build and verify fixes, product updates and new features.
## What We're Looking For
• Pedagogical expertise , especially in scaffolding literacy instruction for struggling readers, special education, and/or multilingual learner education, and ideally from classroom teaching, intervention, instructional coaching or curriculum design.
• Hands-on experience with AI evals , including human labeling, LLM-as-judge rubric design, AI metrics targets definition, and error analysis of LLM outputs.
• AI product fluency : you use LLMs daily and have experience designing complex AI systems for products.
• Experience defining new features and collaborating with engineers to deliver them : you can clearly communicate a problem and solution, and work through technical tradeoffs and UX questions.
• Strong initiative, sharp judgment, and clear writing : you take action when you spot a problem, make swift decisions grounded in data and instincts, and communicate clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
## Nice to Have
• Graduate degree and/or significant direct experience in special education, reading/literacy, ESL/ELD or bilingual education.
• Familiarity with AI eval and observability tools (e.g., LangSmith, Braintrust, Arize, Langfuse) or annotation platforms.
• Proficiency in a language other than English.
• Prior work at an edtech company, or on content quality, assessment design or psychometrics.
• Familiarity with accessibility standards (e.g., WCAG) and assistive technology.
## Why Join Medley
Medley is building products for multilingual learners and students with disabilities, populations that together represent more than 20% of U.S. K-12 students and have historically been underserved by edtech.
You'll join early, work directly with founders and engineering leadership, own meaningful technical and design decisions, and help shape a product that improves access to learning for students nationwide.

We’re hiring a senior Software Engineer in Test to lead how Netflix tests the experiences members use on their TVs and phones. You’ll define what quality means for complex, fast-moving features, build the tools and automation that prove it, and help every engineer around you ship with confidence.
The Teams
Live UI
The Discovery and Viewing Experience (DVX) Live team owns the UI engineering and architecture that powers Live viewing experiences across TV, iOS, and Android. Members show up for live events once, with no second airing and no patch mid-show, so every feature we build is a promise that it will work at that moment on every device that tunes in. As our senior SDET, you’ll lead the way we test Live: recreating the moments a live event creates, like a vote opening just as an ad ends, long before the event does, so we know we’re ready instead of finding out during the show.
What we’re working on:
• The FIFA Women's World Cup, coming to Netflix in 2027 and 2031, will feature new experiences built for global, multi-match sport tournaments.
• Interactive and navigational features that help members move through a live event and catch the moments that matter.
• Real-time voting, which lets members influence a live show as it unfolds, alongside millions of others watching at the same moment.
Mobile Core
The DVX Mobile Core team develops and advances the architecture of Netflix's Android member app. We leverage systems and infrastructure widely available at Netflix and determine the best way to adopt and apply them on Android, enabling easier, more efficient patterns for downstream product engineering teams.
What we’re working on:
• Modernizing our app architecture for the iOS and Android member app. This involves driving migrations and a cross-platform Player rewrite, creating leverage for product teams to ship faster and more reliably on iOS and Android.
• Driving Quality of Experience (QoE). Owning monitoring and performance improvements across Player UI and canvases, as we scale.
The Role
Problem you’ll help solve:
• Testing and making sure millions of members see our Live-specific UI features and capabilities at the right moment, on every TV and phone.
• Giving every platform the same test plan, so TV, iOS, and Android are consistently validated the same way.
• Making tests reliable enough that PMs, designers, engineers, and our partners trust them, and fast enough to run on every change.
• Keeping quality steady while the iOS and Android apps modernize, including a cross-platform player rewrite, so faster delivery doesn’t come with more regressions.
What you’ll do:
• Lead testing for complex features across platforms. Agree on one test plan per feature that teams can trust and validate together, and implement it on TV, iOS, and Android, rather than reconciling differences afterward.
• Build automation that people trust. Evolve our test systems and CI integration across platforms so tests are fast and reliable.
• Make tricky live moments easy to test. Build ways to recreate them on demand instead of waiting for a real event, using mocks, overrides, real devices, and test data that looks like a real event and doesn’t expire.
• Make large migrations safe. Build the test strategy that lets the iOS and Android apps modernize without regressions reaching members
• Own quality metrics. Track how well we’re covered, how reliable our tests are, and which bugs reach members, and use that to decide what to improve next. That includes the client metrics that reveal problems only scale shows, and the alerts that tell us about them quickly.
• Make sure bugs only surprise us once. When a bug reaches members, make sure it comes back as a test, using agents to turn each finding into several, and document how to test each feature so the knowledge doesn’t live in one person’s head.

## About the role:
Cresta’s AI Receptionist answers the phone for small businesses that would otherwise miss the call. It handles millions of conversations a month today, making sure no call goes unanswered and helping owners complete the front-office tasks that keep their business running, and it does so across hundreds of customers. Whether those conversations are actually good is the single most important question in the business, and it deserves a full-time owner. That’s you.
As our first AI Agent Evaluation Engineer, you define what quality means for every agent we run, you build the systems that measure it across every conversation, and you are the person the company trusts when the question is “how good is it, really?”
The work combines hands-on conversation analysis, rigorous evaluation design, and engineering execution: reading and annotating real conversations to learn how the agent actually fails, building the automated evaluation systems (LLM-based judges, golden sets, regression suites) that measure those failures at scale, and keeping those systems honest by calibrating them against human judgment. Fixing what you find is welcome but not the core of the job; an accurate, prioritized picture of agent quality is.
What You'll Do :
## Evaluation Design & Quality Definition
• Define and maintain the evaluation rubric for the agent across three axes: adherence (did it follow its design, call the right tools, respect guardrails), outcome (did the conversation achieve its goal), and conversation experience (latency, turn-taking, tone, repetition).
• Write the annotation guidelines and failure taxonomy the team uses to talk about failures precisely; run calibration sessions and measure inter-rater agreement.
• Classify and prioritize failure modes by severity and frequency so engineering and product work on what matters most.
## Conversation Analysis & Annotation
• Review production conversations by hand every week, leverage QA partners; open-code failures, cluster them, and turn the clusters into the evaluations worth automating.
• Trace each failure to its likely cause (prompt, knowledge gap, tool or flow bug, speech recognition) and route it to the right owner with enough evidence to act on.
• Evaluate across languages and report quality by segment (language, accent, audio quality, intent), not just in aggregate.
## Scalable Evaluation Systems
• Build and operate the evaluation pipeline that scores every production conversation, combining automated checks, LLM-based judges, and human review.
• Calibrate every automated judge against human labels before trusting it; treat judge error as the primary measurement risk.
• Design sampling strategies (stratified by intent, language, caller type, audio conditions) so that reported changes in quality are real.
• Build and maintain the golden set and regression suite that every prompt, model, knowledge, and flow change is validated against before release.
## Coverage & Edge Cases
• Maintain the failure-mode coverage map: which behaviors are tested, partially tested, or unmeasured; close the gaps.
• Design evaluations for behaviors no standard harness covers: high-stakes conversation types such as handoffs to a human, misuse and unwanted-caller handling, and resilience under upstream failures.
• Define the quality and latency thresholds the agent is held to.
## Reporting & Cross-Functional Collaboration
• Report quality trends to internal stakeholders and customers clearly, with uncertainty stated and without burying bad news.
• Partner with forward-deployed engineers, backend engineers, product managers, and the voice/language engineering team to turn findings into prioritized recommendations.
• Document methodology so results are reproducible and the evaluation practice outlives any one person.
## What We're Looking For:
• 3+ years of professional experience in software engineering, applied ML, or data-intensive research roles, including at least 1–2 years working hands-on with LLM-based systems in production.
• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computational Linguistics, Cognitive Science, Statistics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
• Built and operated an end-to-end evaluation system for a production LLM product (agent or otherwise): rubric, human labels, automated judge, regression suite.
• Deep understanding of evaluation methodology: what golden sets, judges, regression suites, and calibration are for, and when each fails. Tool-agnostic; you will work in our in-house tooling.
• Fluent in how LLM agents work: prompts, tool calls, context handling, multi-turn state. You can read a trace and tell what the agent was doing and why.
• Strong programming skills in Python and experience with LLM APIs; able to build and ship evaluation tooling independently. Fine-tuning and ML frameworks are not required.
• Able to write a rubric that independent reviewers would score the same way, and to measure whether they do.
• Able to design a test from an open-ended quality question: you decide what to measure and how, rather than executing a predefined plan.
• Willing to do non-scalable work weekly, both yourself and by directing our QA partners: listening to calls, labeling conversations, building a failure taxonomy from scratch.
• Professional fluency in at least one language other than English, sufficient to evaluate multilingual agent behavior directly.
• Strong written communication; you author the guidelines others follow.
Note on Our Hiring Process
We highly value your time and engineering craftsmanship. To ensure a streamlined and objective process, the first step for qualified applicants following an initial resume review is a self-paced CoderPad technical assessment. This allows you to showcase your practical coding and problem-solving skills in a real-world environment before moving into conversational interview rounds.

## Quality Engineer, Mobile, Audience Experience
About This Role
As a Quality Engineer at BibleProject, you empower teams to ship reliable, secure, and performant software by embedding quality practices throughout the development lifecycle. You lead with automation and observability, design for testability, and partner with Engineers, Product, and Design to shift quality left so that defects are prevented, not just detected. You'll design, build, and own the app's automation suite, identify where coverage is needed across the test pyramid and partner with engineers to close the gaps, and use production signals to target risk — bringing demonstrated experience driving quality for production software at scale.
The App squad owns the BibleProject mobile app, where our audience reads and studies Scripture, often in community. Quality is what makes that experience trustworthy, and mobile makes that its own kind of challenge: the app has to hold up offline or on a weak connection, across a wide range of iOS and Android devices. You'll be the quality owner and anchor for this squad, working independently and shaping how we build for quality early rather than waiting to be handed test cases. That matters especially right now: we're building toward the future of the app, and testability is still something we can shape as we go. Manual testing here is targeted exploratory discovery — the critical and edge cases, the accessibility gaps, the things automation won't catch — rather than high-volume regression.
Most importantly, you'll be an integral part of maturing the product engineering culture of BibleProject, setting and maintaining a high bar with regard to our standards and people, and working to create an environment where great technical professionals like yourself can ship work worthy of our mission at a sustainable pace that reflects the BibleProject values: creative, humble, thoughtful, unifying, generous, and unhurried.
Core Functions
Leadership
• Own the App squad's automation suite and quality roadmap independently — build, maintain, and evolve it without ongoing pairing support.
• Own test strategy across the pyramid: identify where tests are needed — unit, component, integration, end-to-end — and partner with engineers to close gaps, influencing scope and sequencing based on risk and user impact.
• Champion shift-left practices: drive testability in design reviews and codify quality engineering standards and patterns.
• Partner with Product, Design, DevOps, and Data to define testable acceptance criteria (usability, accessibility, offline/edge-case behavior) and align on SLOs and release readiness.
• Drive continuous improvement: identify bottlenecks in CI/CD, observability, and environments, and deliver measurable fixes.
Responsibilities
• Build and maintain the automation suite with durable patterns, stable test data, and reliable test environments across iOS and Android.
• Track coverage gaps as the product evolves, and partner with engineers to get unit and component-level tests written and maintained in the codebase.
• Integrate tests into CI/CD with clear gates, fast feedback, and actionable reporting, driving down flaky failures over time.
• Plan and execute targeted exploratory testing on critical flows, new designs, and edge cases — offline/poor-connectivity behavior, accessibility gaps, and other issues automation won't catch — documenting reproducible steps and user impact.
• Establish, track, and improve quality signals (defect rate, change-failure rate, test stability, coverage depth, crash-free rate); validate releases using production signals and lead post-release verification for high-risk launches.
Expertise
• Mobile test automation: hands-on building and maintaining mobile UI automation suites from durable, maintainable patterns rather than one-offs; experience with Appium and the Page Object Model is a plus.
• Observability and analysis: using logs, metrics, traces, and crash reporting to validate behavior and identify defects quickly.
• Mobile quality judgment: offline and poor-connectivity correctness, behavior across a wide device range, mobile performance budgets and their user impact, and the release constraints of shipping through app stores.
• Product fluency for mobile: fluent in iOS and Android conventions, able to identify and articulate why something that technically passes still violates expected user experience.
• UX, accessibility, and AI-assisted quality: practical accessibility techniques for mobile and qualitative usability methods, plus comfort using AI-assisted tools to generate test ideas and data, summarize signals, and draft reports with human review and privacy-safe handling.
What We're Looking For
• 5+ years of experience (or equivalent skill) building and maintaining automated tests and quality tooling in a product team, including production software at scale.
• Demonstrated ability to build and own a mobile automation suite independently — designing stable tests, integrating them into a delivery pipeline, and driving down flakiness — without ongoing pairing support.
• Track record of risk-based coverage analysis: identifying where tests add the most value across a product and partnering with engineers to close gaps.
• Proven experience using production signals and observability to guide testing strategy and risk mitigation.
• Demonstrated ability to translate usability, accessibility, and performance expectations into testable acceptance criteria.
• Track record of surfacing blockers early and driving them to resolution without recurring escalation.
• Track record of giving and incorporating feedback, with demonstrated growth in scope of ownership over time.
• Alignment with BibleProject's mission and values.

Portland, Oregon, Founded in 2014
BibleProject is an educational technology and media studio whose mission is to help people experience the Bible as a unified story that leads to Jesus.
We have grown significantly in the area of multimedia technology. What began with two animated videos now encompasses multiple platforms and products—including over 200 videos. The QA Lead is accountable for the quality assurance practice across product delivery, ensuring that software is testable, test execution is timely and transparent, critical defects are surfaced early, and releases meet agreed quality standards. This role leads day-to-day QA planning and execution, strengthens automation and regression coverage, coaches QA team members, and works closely with Product Owners and Engineering to embed quality throughout the software development lifecycle rather than treating testing as a final-stage activity.
The QA Lead is expected to create clear visibility into test readiness, progress, risk, and blockers. The role owns the operating discipline of QA: defining test approaches, ensuring execution begins when planned, maintaining useful quality metrics, driving defect triage, and escalating issues early when delivery or release quality is at risk.
Key Responsibilities
Quality Leadership & Accountability
• Own the day-to-day QA practice and establish consistent expectations for test planning, execution, documentation, and release readiness.
• Ensure QA work begins when planned and that delays, blockers, environment issues, data needs, or scope gaps are identified and communicated immediately.
• Create transparency into what has been tested, what remains untested, current defects, quality risks, and confidence in release readiness.
• Hold QA team members accountable for execution commitments, timely updates, accurate status reporting, and follow-through.
• Coach QA team members on testing discipline, risk-based thinking, root-cause analysis, and stronger ownership of outcomes.
Test Strategy, Planning & Execution
• Develop and maintain test strategies for new features, enhancements, integrations, defects, and platform changes.
• Partner with Product Owners early in discovery and refinement to identify test scenarios, edge cases, data needs, dependencies, and acceptance criteria before development is complete.
• Ensure test cases provide adequate functional, integration, regression, negative, end-to-end, and workflow coverage based on business and technical risk.
• Coordinate test data, environments, integrations, and dependencies required for successful QA execution.
• Confirm that critical workflows can be tested end-to-end before work is considered ready for business UAT.
• Use risk-based testing to prioritize the highest-value scenarios when time or environment constraints require tradeoffs.
Defect Management & Release Readiness
• Lead defect triage in partnership with Product and Engineering, ensuring severity, priority, business impact, and ownership are clear.
• Track critical defects through resolution and retest and ensure unresolved quality risks are explicitly documented before release decisions.
• Define and enforce practical QA exit criteria, including expectations for critical defect closure, regression completion, and stability.
• Provide an objective quality recommendation for releases based on test evidence and known risk.
• Identify recurring defect patterns and partner with Engineering and Product on preventive actions rather than relying only on downstream testing.
Automation & Continuous Improvement
• Develop and maintain a pragmatic test automation strategy focused on high-value regression, repeatable workflows, integrations, and business-critical scenarios.
• Partner with QA Automation Engineers and Engineering to increase reliable automated coverage without creating brittle or low-value automation.

Cross-Functional Partnership
• Work closely with Product Owners to ensure requirements and acceptance criteria are clear, testable, and aligned to expected business outcomes.
• Partner with Engineering on defect prevention, unit/integration test expectations, environment stability, observability, and root-cause analysis.

Why work at PaceMate?
Recognized as a Top 100 Healthcare Technology Company by Healthcare Technology Report, PaceMate is one of the nation’s fastest-growing companies in cardiac rhythm management software and remote monitoring. Combining the most technologically advanced cloud-native software, research-grade data, and seamless integrations, PaceMateLIVE™, the company’s flagship remote monitoring software platform, is enabling many of the nation’s most renowned electrophysiologists, device clinics, and healthcare systems to effectively manage their device patient populations. With PaceMate, healthcare organizations can experience comprehensive interoperability and secure data exchange—significantly improving patient outcomes, reimbursements, and productivity.
Join our team
Joining the PaceMate™ Team means becoming a vital part of a group that is dedicated to using technology to benefit patients, caregivers, and hospital administrators while driving healthy turnkey solutions that identify lost revenues and inefficiencies.
PaceMate is looking for a Product Validation Lead to own the final step of our product lifecycle: turning a PRD and user stories into a validated, trustworthy release. Our Engineering QA team verifies that we built the software right. This role verifies that we built the right thing — that every release does what we promised, for real clinic users, at acceptable speed.
This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role with real authority: you hold formal go/no-go sign-off on every release. You'll own UAT, frontend and usability testing, and product performance standards, while partnering closely with Engineering QA on coverage and defect triage. AI fluency is core to this role — you'll use AI tools to generate and prioritize test coverage, paired with the sharp, skeptical judgment to know when that output can't be trusted.
This is a fully remote position open to candidates residing anywhere in the contiguous United States.
## What You'll Do
• Own the release gate: deliver a documented go/no-go recommendation every 1-2 weeks, with any Chief Product Officer override documented when used.
• Plan and run UAT cycles from user stories — recruiting, coaching, and coordinating Customer Success, clinical, and customer testers, and turning their feedback into clear, actionable defects.
• Select, build, and maintain frontend end-to-end test automation (e.g., Playwright or Cypress) for critical clinic workflows, and run it in CI.
• Use our PRD-to-test-case pipeline and AI tools to generate, review, prune, and prioritize test coverage, applying human judgment wherever AI output isn't trustworthy.
• Define and own product performance standards — page load, time to interactive, and critical workflow response times — measuring every release and escalating regressions.
• Evaluate usability, accessibility, and workflow friction that functional testing doesn't catch.
• Review PRDs and acceptance criteria before development starts, flagging untestable, ambiguous, or missing requirements back to Product.
• Partner with Engineering QA on a shared coverage map, joint defect triage, and release gates.
• Maintain non-PHI test data and validation environments that reflect real manufacturer and device variety.
• Report release quality to the Chief Product Officer, including UAT pass rate, escaped defects, coverage, and performance trends.
• Help shape playbooks, tooling standards, and the hiring profile for future Product Validation team members.
## What You'll Need
• 5+ years in QA, UAT, or product quality, with recent hands-on test automation experience.
• Experience writing and maintaining end-to-end tests in Playwright, Cypress, or a similar framework, integrated into CI.
• Experience running UAT with non-technical or customer-facing testers.
• Practical frontend performance experience (Lighthouse, Core Web Vitals, WebPageTest, or real-user monitoring).
• Current, hands-on use of AI tools for test generation, with a critical eye on their output.
• Ability to read a PRD and identify untestable or missing requirements before development starts.
• Strong written communication skills, with the judgment to hold a release gate under deadline pressure.
## Nice to Have
• Experience in healthcare or regulated software, including familiarity with HIPAA, validation documentation, and audit readiness.
• Familiarity with clinical workflows, cardiac devices, or remote monitoring.
• Accessibility testing experience (WCAG 2.1 AA).

Review websites and documents to define audit scope, representative pages, user workflows, document complexity, and effort estimates; support proposals and statements of work.
Run automated accessibility testing, investigate reported issues, resolve false positives, and perform manual checks for requirements that automated tools cannot reliably assess.
Test keyboard navigation, focus order and visibility, keyboard traps, menus, dialogs, forms, error handling, and dynamic content across agreed browsers and devices.

Explain audit results to clients and developers, prioritize corrective actions, and provide practical guidance on accessible content authoring and remediation.
Prepare audit summaries, report cards, punch lists, and Accessibility Conformance Reports using approved VPAT templates when included in scope; accurately describe test coverage and limitations.
Participate in peer reviews, maintain test evidence and file versions, track assignments and turnaround times, and protect confidential client information.
Collaborate with Lighthouse developers and accessibility testers to improve internal and client solutions; maintain knowledge of relevant standards, techniques, and testing tools.

We are looking for an early-career systems engineer who likes figuring out what a system actually needs to do and then proving that it does. You’ll sit down with the operators who use DoD mission systems every day, turn what they tell you into clear, testable requirements, and write the test procedures that operators and developers use to verify each release. Just as important, you’ll explain why a request should or shouldn’t be built, and stand behind that recommendation. Our purpose is singular — to optimize warfighter performance
through information technology.
We hire for talent and drive over years on a résumé. Strong recent graduates are encouraged to apply.
You have…
• A clear, structured voice. You can walk someone through a problem — the situation, the options you weighed, what you decided, and the result so operators, engineers, and leaders follow it the first time.
• A curious mind. You want to understand how a system is really used, not just how it was designed.
• A good ear and good judgment. You listen for what operators need versus what they ask for, weigh it against technical constraints and the backlog, and can tell a customer “not now” while pointing them to a better path.
• An ownership mindset. When something is blocked, you go find the person who can unblock it instead of waiting.
• A dedication to detail. A vague requirement becomes a bug or a dispute later, so you pin it down now.
• A focus on the craft. You want to go deep in systems engineering and software requirements, test, and how software actually gets built.
• An open mind. You welcome feedback on your work and want to grow as an engineer.
We have…
• A devotion to making technology work for the warfighter. We help operators work faster, better, and smarter.
• An affinity to action. We’d rather start, learn, and iterate than wait for the perfect plan.
• A drive for continuous improvement. We look for better ways to solve old problems, for our customers and ourselves.
• Senior engineers who mentor. You’ll learn requirements and test practice alongside experienced test leads and SMEs.

Requirements elicitation and decomposition
Run discovery with operators, subject matter experts, and government leads, through interviews, site visits, and demos, to understand mission workflows, pain points, and what would make a capability acceptable to them.
• Decompose customer-expressed and contract requirements into clear, atomic, testable requirements, breaking large asks into smaller parts that can be weighed against effort to implement.
• Trace requirements across subsystems and interfaces (APIs, data exchanges, connected systems) and assess the ripple effect of each change.
• Capture non-functional requirements (the “-ilities”): performance, reliability, security, and operation in degraded or disconnected (DDIL) conditions.
• Maintain requirements traceability from source (operator input, PWS, user stories) through design and test.
Operator input and prioritization
• Capture every operator or customer request as a data point: log it in the backlog, link it to existing requirements, and track it to a decision.
• Weigh requests against mission value, technical constraints, and the existing backlog; recommend build, defer, or decline, and explain why.
• Reconcile conflicting inputs from different operators or stakeholders and bring a recommended resolution to the team.
• Close the loop with operators on what was decided and when.
Documentation
• Document requirements, use cases, and operational workflows in formats operators and developers both understand.
• Write user stories with measurable acceptance criteria, including Given-When-Then (Gherkin) scenarios.
• Use quick prototypes or mockups (including AI-assisted ones) to confirm intent with operators and show developers the target outcome, without dictating how they build it.
• Produce supporting artifacts: workflow and system diagrams, Technical Exchange Meeting (TEM) minutes, and test reports.
Test planning and execution
• Write step-by-step test procedures and scripts that operators and developers can follow to verify functionality.
• Execute and support functional, regression, integration, and user acceptance testing (UAT) for software releases.
• Record results, log defects with clear reproduction steps, and verify fixes.
• Help automate repeatable testing: write simple scripts for test data and log checks, turn manual procedures into automated test cases and BDD step definitions.
• Contribute to functional security test cases (authentication, access control).
Collaboration
• Work alongside developers, test leads, cybersecurity staff, and program management in an Agile environment.
• Coordinate across multiple organizations and drive communication plans that keep responses and deliverables on schedule.

• Contribute technical writing to proposals as opportunities arise.

## About Practifi (The Real Story)
Practifi is the only intelligent CRM company that meets wealth management firms wherever they are in their AI adoption journey. Our enterprise-grade, compliance-first foundation brings client data, workflows, and relationship intelligence together in one system, so firms can understand what matters, take the right action, and scale without ever needing a new CRM.
That same directness runs through how we work. We're a team of fewer than 100 people, remote-first across the US and Australia, and we'd rather tell you how this job actually works than polish it for the pitch. We don't sell a version of the role that doesn't exist.
## The Opportunity (What This Role Really Means)
When a wealth management firm moves onto Practifi, the first thing they judge us on is their data. If a household is missing a member, if a client shows up twice, or if a servicing team points to the wrong advisor, they notice on day one. So do their clients.
Right now, quality assurance on those data migrations is handled by whoever is delivering the engagement, on top of everything else on their plate. It works, but it means every client gets a slightly different process and nobody has a clear view of the issues that keep coming back.
We're creating this role to change that. As our Data QA Analyst, you'll be the dedicated owner of data migration quality across every client onboarding engagement. You'll work the checklist object by object, build one standard the whole team uses, and spot the patterns a single-project view misses. You'll be a big part of why a client's first login feels like their business, not a spreadsheet import.
## Your Day-to-Day (The Honest Version)
The Core Work
• Validate every migration end to end. You'll analyze source data (record counts, missing values, duplicates, orphaned contacts, inconsistent values), then walk through the Practifi interface object by object to confirm everything displays and connects the way the client's Data Mapping Document says it should.
• Check the details that matter. Every record carries a valid External Id and Batch Id, nothing is owned by a default system user, every contact is tied to at least one relationship, and counts reconcile to source or have a clear explanation.
• Log, route, and retest. You'll capture screenshots of failed checks, log findings in Asana and JIRA, route fixes to engineering, and retest once they're corrected.
• Report clearly. After each Initial Load and Final Load, you'll give the Project Manager, Consultant, or Business Analyst the metrics they need, and you'll prepare the final QA sign-off report before go-live.
• Raise the flag early. When a data issue puts a go-live at risk, you'll escalate it to the Project Manager within 24 hours
• Build the standard. You'll own one QA checklist and issue-tracking format for every engagement, replacing the client-by-client workbooks in use today, and you'll track recurring issues across clients so we fix the process, not just the record.
The Reality Check
The Practifi data model has its own vocabulary, and it takes time to learn how it all fits together. You won't figure it out alone. You'll complete the same onboarding and training curriculum as every individual contributor here, including our PractifiU learning platform, and you'll have a Practibuddy mentor from day one.
You'll also be working alongside Consultants, Business and Data Analysts, Data Engineers, and Project Managers. Part of the job is raising problems in a way that keeps projects moving. And when QA volume is lighter, you'll flex into delivery support, so you'll see the whole implementation, not just your portion of it.
The Growth
This is a new role, which means you'll shape it. The checklist, the reporting format, and the process improvements you contribute each quarter become part of how Data Services operates.
You'll earn a Salesforce certification once you're here, with time and support built in, and an annual Learnbucks stipend for the courses and certifications you choose after that. We promote from within. A role that sees every engagement is a strong foundation for a path into consulting, data engineering, or delivery leadership.
## What We're Really Looking For
The Must-Haves
• 3 to 5 years of experience in data quality, data migration, data validation, or quality assurance, ideally in a CRM or software environment
• Hands-on experience reconciling data: comparing record counts, running field-by-field checks, and finding duplicate and orphaned records
• Comfort working inside Salesforce or a comparable CRM, navigating objects, records, and related lists
• A working understanding of how relational data fits together (IDs, lookups, and records that link other records)
• Experience logging and tracking issues in JIRA, Asana, or a similar tool
• Clear written communication, including findings a non-technical stakeholder can act on
The Nice-to-Haves
• Experience with Salesforce Inspector, the Salesforce Developer Console, Data Loader, or SOQL queries
• Background in wealth management, financial services, or another regulated industry
• Experience supporting client onboarding or software implementation projects
• Strong spreadsheet skills (lookups, pivot tables, conditional formatting)
A Salesforce certification isn't required to apply. You'll earn one with us.
The More Important Stuff
• You’re observant and tuned into the details within the data.
• You care about the cause of an issue, not just the fix.
• You're comfortable telling a Project Manager something they don't want to hear, and you do it early and kindly.
• You like building structure where there isn't any yet.
• You're honest about what you don't know and curious enough to go find out.
## What Taking This Leap Gets You
The Practical Stuff
• Base salary: $78,000 to $95,000. We share the range because you deserve to know it before you apply. Where you land depends on your experience against the role.
• Generous time off: 20 days of paid vacation, 10 sick days, 3 personal days, and 3 volunteering days annually
• Medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance benefits, plus a 401(k) with company match
• Fully remote within the US
The Cultural Stuff
• A Practibuddy mentor from your first day, so you always have someone to ask
• An annual Learnbucks education stipend for the courses and certifications you choose
• Bi-annual in-person summits in Chicago where the whole company gets together
• A Slack culture where questions are welcome and wins get celebrated
• Remote-first that's real: genuine work-life integration, not a line in a job ad
## Living Our Values Daily
• Growth: You'll be part of building a function from the ground up, with Learnbucks and a real promotion path behind you.
• Collaboration: You'll partner with every delivery role on every engagement, and the fix is always a team effort.
• Transparency: The salary is in this ad, and your QA findings will be shared openly, good news and bad.

Your evaluations will help identify where current machine learning models perform effectively and where their outputs require further refinement.
This opportunity is suited to experienced researchers, academics, data analysts, technical writers, and domain specialists who can critically assess complex information, identify factual inaccuracies, and provide structured, evidence-based feedback.
Requirements
## Key Responsibilities
• Review machine learning model outputs generated in response to a range of research-focused and domain-specific prompts.
• Evaluate AI-generated responses for factual accuracy, relevance, completeness, and overall quality.
• Assess the technical validity and reliability of information presented in model-generated responses.
• Use a structured rating system to evaluate and score responses consistently.
• Provide concise, clear, and well-reasoned written justifications supporting evaluation scores.
• Identify factual errors, gaps in reasoning, irrelevant information, and areas requiring improvement.
• Complete approximately five hours of independent evaluation work asynchronously.
• Maintain consistency and attention to detail throughout the evaluation process.
## Required Qualifications and Skills
• PhD or equivalent advanced subject matter expertise in a relevant academic, technical, or professional discipline.
• Strong academic or professional background in a specialised domain, with the ability to assess complex information critically.
• Excellent analytical, research, and critical-thinking skills.
• Ability to evaluate technical content, research findings, and domain-specific information for factual correctness and relevance.
• Strong written communication skills, particularly in providing clear and structured evaluation justifications.
• High attention to detail and the ability to identify subtle inaccuracies, inconsistencies, and gaps in AI-generated responses.
• Ability to work independently and complete approximately five hours of asynchronous evaluation tasks.
## Suitable Candidate Profiles
Professionals from the following backgrounds are encouraged to apply:
• Academic researchers and university faculty
• PhD scholars and doctoral-level subject matter experts
• Data analysts and research analysts
• Technical writers and research professionals
• Domain specialists with experience evaluating technical or research-focused content
## Engagement and Payment Terms
• Contract Type: Independent contractor engagement.
• Work Arrangement: Fully remote, with flexible working hours.
• Project Duration: Approximately five hours of evaluation work.
• Payment: Payments are processed weekly based on services rendered.
• Project Continuity: The engagement may be extended, shortened, or concluded early depending on project requirements and individual performance.
• Confidentiality: Participation will not require access to confidential or proprietary information belonging to any current or former employer, client, or academic institution.
• Work Authorisation: H-1B and STEM OPT candidates cannot be supported for this opportunity.
## Interview and Evaluation Expectations
During the interview process, candidates may be assessed on their review practices, critical thinking, and ability to improve the quality of their evaluations. Responses should address the following three habits:
• Exchanging unfinished review notes with another reviewer.
• Maintaining a separate log of opinions or assessments that have changed during the review process.
• Using review notes and feedback to update personal reading lists.
## Ideal Candidate Profile
The ideal candidate combines deep subject matter expertise with strong research judgement and analytical precision. They should be comfortable reviewing complex AI-generated content, distinguishing accurate information from flawed reasoning, and communicating their assessments through clear, structured feedback.

Owns the quality engineering function for an agentic conversational AI platform — serving as the guardian of the customer experience across every voice and chat interaction. This role spans two mandates: hands-on assurance that every release is effective and defect-free before it reaches end users, and building, scaling, and maintaining the evaluation infrastructure that makes quality continuous, measurable, and increasingly self-improving.
The role plans and directs the development, application, and maintenance of quality standards for conversational AI applications and their supporting systems and owns the automated evaluation platform — synthetic and adversarial agent-to-agent conversation testing, DeepEval test suites, proprietary LLM-as-judge evaluators, and deterministic rule-based checks — as the system of record for shipping model, prompt, and agent changes with confidence. Because LLM systems are non-deterministic, this role designs test plans and evaluation rubrics that turn ambiguous notions of quality into clear, defensible metrics, and correlates those metrics with real-world performance and user experience.
